claim: Within one LLM and across LLMs, open-ended answers are homogeneous (the Artificial Hivemind effect), and LLM judges and reward models track individual human tastes poorly where tastes differ.
quote: language models, reward models, and LM judges are less well calibrated to human ratings when annotators have differing idiosyncratic preferences
authors: Jiang, Chai, Li, Liu, Fok, Dziri, Tsvetkov, Sap, Albalak, Choi
title: Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
n: 26K queries, 31,250 human annotations, 25 raters per item
transfer: Do not use a second sample or a second model from the same family as a source of different ideas. Use an explicit diversity step and a non-LLM or multi-criteria pruning signal; do not trust an LLM judge to rank novelty.

claim: Frontier LLMs give much less diverse answers than human writers; larger models within a family are often less diverse than smaller ones.
quote: larger models within a family often exhibit less diversity than their smaller counterparts
authors: Zhang, Diddee, Holm, Liu, Liu, Samuel, Wang, Ippolito
title: NoveltyBench: Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity
n: 20 models, 100 curated prompts, 8 human answers each
transfer: Matches our own NoveltyBench result (3.18 distinct of 10 plain). Supports a forced-divergence route for open prompts. Prefer in-context regeneration (show prior answers, ask for different) as the cheap baseline.

claim: Asking the model for a set of responses with stated probabilities (verbalized sampling) raises diversity in creative writing by 1.6 to 2.1 times over direct prompting, with more capable models gaining more.
quote: in creative writing, VS increases diversity by 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting
authors: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning, Shi
title: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
n: several tasks, many models; exact n not checked
transfer: Step: in one call, ask for k candidate answers each with a probability, then sample from the low-probability tail. One call replaces k correlated calls. Use only on open-ended routes.

claim: VS authors attribute mode collapse partly to typicality bias in human preference data: annotators favor familiar text.
title: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
transfer: Explains why the first natural answer is the typical one: a step that explicitly asks for atypical candidates works against the training pressure.

claim: LLMs fixate like humans: early outputs narrow later ideas. Chain-of-thought reduced fixation in LLMs but not in humans. Ordinary personas gave more partitioned knowledge than creative-expert personas. CoT plus ordinary personas gave more diverse ideas than human samples.
title: Examining and Addressing Barriers to Diversity in LLM-Generated Ideas
n: four studies; sizes not on abstract page
transfer: Step: generate ideas in separate fresh calls (no earlier ideas in context) with a different ordinary persona or knowledge domain each, and reason before answering. Avoids in-context fixation.

claim: Independent LLM samples are less diverse than independent human samples, because LLMs blend knowledge into one distribution rather than partitioning it across regions as a human population does.
title: Examining and Addressing Barriers to Diversity in LLM-Generated Ideas
transfer: Partition the idea space by hand: a program lists distinct domains, stakeholders or mechanisms, and each call is assigned one. This is a structured-imagination step with explicit categories.

claim: In a randomized study, writers given LLM story ideas produced stories rated more novel (+5.4% with 1 idea, +8.1% with 5) and more useful, but the stories were more similar to each other. Low-creativity writers gained most.
quote: These results point to an increase in individual creativity at the risk of losing collective novelty.
title: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content
transfer: An LLM idea is a good seed for one thinker but a trap for a population. For one agent that repeats itself over many problems, track idea similarity across runs and penalise repeats in the lessons ledger.

claim: Expert blind reviewers rated LLM research ideas as more novel than expert human ideas, slightly weaker on feasibility; the authors report weak LLM self-evaluation and low diversity in generated ideas.
quote: LLM-generated ideas are judged as more novel (p < 0.05) than human expert ideas
title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
transfer: Generate many ideas then rank is useful, but the ranker (the LLM itself) is weak. Rank with an outside check or a separate rubric and dedupe before ranking.

claim: When 43 experts executed randomly assigned LLM or human ideas, LLM ideas lost significantly more score after execution on all metrics, and rankings often flipped in favour of human ideas.
quote: the scores of the LLM-generated ideas decrease significantly more than expert-written ideas on all evaluation metrics
title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
n: 43 researchers, about 103 hours each, 7 NLP topics
transfer: Novelty judged on paper overstates value. Add an explore step that tests an idea against a real check (run, simulate, constraint test) before it is kept. Matches our architecture-search win where a training run judged.

claim: LLMs can beat the average human on the Divergent Association Task and approach human creative writing, but remain below highly creative humans; the paper proposes prompt design and hyperparameters to raise semantic diversity.
quote: surpass average human performance on the Divergent Association Task
authors: Bellemare-Pepin, Lespinasse, Thoelke, Harel, Mathewson, Olson, Bengio, Jerbi and others
title: Divergent Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models
transfer: Average-level word divergence is cheap; the gap is at the top tail. Use a semantic-distance measure (embedding distance between candidates) as a program-side filter, not a model opinion.

claim: Temperature is only weakly correlated with novelty (and moderately with incoherence) in narrative generation, so it is not a real creativity dial; the authors call for more controlled ways to get creative output.
quote: temperature is weakly correlated with novelty, and unsurprisingly, moderately correlated with incoherence
title: Is Temperature the Creativity Parameter of Large Language Models?
transfer: Do not use temperature as the divergence step. Use structural prompts (different seeds, constraints, personas, domains) instead. Single model and task, so test it ourselves.

claim: Interaction structure matters more than agent count in multi-agent idea generation: authority-led groups gave less semantic diversity than junior-led groups, adding agents has diminishing returns, and dense communication makes ideas converge early.
quote: authority-driven dynamics suppress semantic diversity compared to junior-dominated groups
authors: Chen, Tong, Yang, He, Zhang, Zou, Wang, He
title: Diversity Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Structural Coupling and Collective Failure in Open-Ended Idea Generation
transfer: For a single agent with many calls: generate ideas in isolated calls, merge only after. Never let a strong first idea lead the rest. Keep disagreement, do not let an editor call smooth it away.

claim: In two pre-registered experiments, LLM help may hinder independent creative performance when users later work without assistance.
quote: it may inadvertently hinder independent creative performance when users work without assistance
title: Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs: Randomized Experiments on Divergent and Convergent Thinking
transfer: Weak for agents. Analogy: an agent that always reads its own earlier outputs may lose independent variation; hold back some generation calls with no memory in context.

claim: On the CREATE associative-creativity benchmark, thinking models are not always better even with large token budgets.
quote: thinking models are not always more effective on our task, even with high token budgets
title: CREATE: Testing LLMs for Associative Creativity
transfer: More reasoning tokens do not buy more associative range. Spend tokens on separate seeded generations and path scoring (specific and different), not on a longer single chain.

claim: CREATE has models produce sets of paths linking concepts and scores them on specificity and diversity, a machine version of an associative-hierarchy test (flat versus steep).
quote: CREATE requires models to generate sets of paths connecting concepts in a model's parametric knowledge.
title: CREATE: Testing LLMs for Associative Creativity
transfer: Step for remote association: for two concepts, list several distinct paths, drop the generic ones, keep the specific and different ones. Can also be used as an offline test of the step.

claim: A search summary of CREATE says classic tests such as the Remote Associates Test are easy for LLMs and likely seen in training (contamination), so RAT scores are a poor measure of LLM creativity.
authors: Wadhwa et al. as summarised in search results (not opened in full)
title: CREATE: Testing LLMs for Associative Creativity
transfer: Do not use RAT items to test our own agent's creative steps; build fresh items.

claim: LiveIdeaBench (40+ models, 1,180 keywords, 22 domains) finds that scientific idea generation from a one-word prompt is poorly predicted by general-intelligence scores.
quote: poorly predicted by standard metrics of general intelligence
authors: Ruan, Wang, Hong, Wang, Liu, Sun
title: Evaluating LLMs' Divergent Thinking Capabilities for Scientific Idea Generation with Minimal Context
n: 40+ models, 1,180 keywords, 22 domains, LLM panel judges
transfer: A model good at puzzles is not automatically good at ideas; choose which call uses which model or prompt per route. Judged by an LLM panel, so treat scores as soft.

claim: A search summary reports a benchmark of 35 LLMs where models are 10 to 16 points better at associations and analogies than at blends, and about one in five invented concepts reuses properties invented by another model. Source paper not confirmed.
authors: unconfirmed (search result for the KOMBINE benchmark)
title: KOMBINE (title as given in a search summary)
venue: not opened; arXiv id not confirmed
transfer: If confirmed, conceptual blending is the weakest combinatorial skill and a blend step needs scaffolding (explicit input spaces, shared structure, emergent-property check). VERIFY before use; the URL is the related Combinatorial Creativity paper, not confirmed to be this one.

claim: An agent that maps combinatorial-creativity theory onto prompting, with retrieval of cross-domain concepts, improved similarity to real research developments by 7 to 10 percent over baselines on OAG-Bench.
authors: Gu et al. (as given in search results)
title: LLMs can Realize Combinatorial Creativity: Generating Creative Ideas via LLMs for Scientific Research
transfer: Step: pull concepts from a different domain by retrieval, then combine. The metric is similarity to later real work, a weak proxy for novelty.

claim: A design-by-analogy experiment with 84 engineering students reportedly found near-field analogies sharing sub-functions with the target gave higher novelty and quality than distant ones for designers without analogy training; the far-analogy advantage is disputed and depends on problem and training.
authors: Becattini, Cascini (as given in search results)
title: design-by-analogy experiment (exact title not confirmed)
transfer: Do not assume far is better. Step: sample analogies at near and far distance and let a check choose. The linked page is the older Chan et al. work, not confirmed to be this study; verify before use.

claim: A white paper reports that persona-conditioned agents replacing a uniform system prompt raised an LLM-judged diversity score by a mean of 4.1 points on a 1 to 10 scale; the authors flag judge bias.
title: The Spark Effect
transfer: Consistent with persona seeding, but judged by an LLM, so weak. Use as a hypothesis to test with embedding distance.

claim: No source found in this round applies Geneplore (generate then explore) directly to LLM agents; the closest work is combinatorial-creativity and generate-then-rank ideation pipelines.
title: Search gap note
transfer: We can state a Geneplore step ourselves (generate preinventive forms, then interpret them under constraints) and test it against our NoveltyBench and architecture runs; there is no outside evidence for it yet.
